incidents.title: Cambodia-based romance-baiting scam uses ChatGPT for multilingual lures
incidents.targets: Social-media users in Japan, China and English markets
incidents.outcome: Victims were drawn into romance and investment scams.
incidents.confidenceReason: OpenAI, the model provider, reports on its own platform in February 2025: "We identified and banned a set of ChatGPT accounts whose activity appeared connected to an operation originating in Cambodia."
incidents.summary: A likely Cambodia-based network used ChatGPT to translate and generate comments in Japanese, Chinese and English for romance and investment scams.
incidents.quote: A likely Cambodia-based network translated and generated comments in Japanese, Chinese and English for romance and investment scams, which OpenAI disrupted alongside a separate Urdu-English task scam.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only OpenAI has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Threat Watch restates.

incidents.title: Italian defence minister's cloned voice used to solicit tycoons
incidents.targets: Italian business leaders (Moratti, Armani, Prada and others)
incidents.outcome: Massimo Moratti reportedly sent nearly EUR 1M; Milan prosecutors froze it. Others did not pay.
incidents.confidenceReason: Euronews headline says AI clone, but its body: 'It is unclear whether Crosetto's voice was a pre-recorded message or a filter created with artificial intelligence'. No victim or prosecutor statement on AI quoted.
incidents.summary: Callers posing as Defence Minister Guido Crosetto asked wealthy Italians for money to free kidnapped journalists. Crosetto filed a complaint.
incidents.quote: Scammers clone Italian defence minister's voice with AI in ransom scheme
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Euronews has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

harness.note: Deepfake/impersonation tool only, no agent harness

incidents.title: DPRK-linked accounts use ChatGPT for intrusion-tool research and RDP brute-force tooling
incidents.actor: Suspected VELVET CHOLLIMA (Kimsuky) and STARDUST CHOLLIMA (APT38) accounts
incidents.targets: Unspecified; interest in cryptocurrency and cyber intrusion tools
incidents.outcome: OpenAI banned the accounts; staging URLs for unknown binaries it found were shared with the security community.
incidents.confidenceReason: OpenAI, the model provider, states the accounts used its models for this work.
incidents.summary: Accounts OpenAI links to Kimsuky (VELVET CHOLLIMA) and BlueNoroff (STARDUST CHOLLIMA) used ChatGPT for coding help, research on intrusion tools, RDP brute-force tooling and RAT development. The date is the report month.
incidents.quote: The banned accounts primarily used our tools to pursue information likely related to cyber intrusion tools or operations.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only OpenAI has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Threat Watch restates.

incidents.title: 中高生の生成ＡＩ悪用事件、「指示役」中３男子「本人確認が甘い楽天狙った」
incidents.outcome: 105 eSIM lines were contracted through about 220,000 unauthorized logins.
incidents.confidenceReason: Yomiuri attributes the generative-AI use to unnamed investigative sources (捜査関係者への取材: "処理速度向上などに生成ＡＩが悪用されていた"). The AI claim rests on an anonymous source, so the grade is Suspected.
incidents.summary: Three teenagers used a credential-stuffing program improved with generative AI to log in to Rakuten Mobile with stolen IDs and contract eSIM lines for resale, from May to August 2024; police announced the arrests in February 2025.
incidents.quote: プログラムは、ＩＤとパスワードを機械的に入力し、契約者と一致すると回線数の上限まで追加契約するもので、処理速度向上などに生成ＡＩが悪用されていた。
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Yomiuri Shimbun has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: Storm-2139 network steals Azure OpenAI customer credentials and resells access to bypass safeguards
incidents.actor: Storm-2139 (global network of creators, providers and users)
incidents.targets: Azure OpenAI and other generative AI service customers whose credentials were scraped
incidents.outcome: Microsoft named members in a civil action; hijacked accounts were used to make harmful imagery and access was resold.
incidents.confidenceReason: Microsoft, the provider whose service was abused, states the facts in its own disclosure and court filing.
incidents.summary: Storm-2139 used exposed customer credentials to hijack Azure OpenAI accounts, alter their safeguards and resell access to generate harmful images. Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit sued. Activity from late 2024; disclosed February 2025.
incidents.quote: Members of Storm-2139 exploited exposed customer credentials scraped from public sources to unlawfully access accounts with certain generative AI services.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Microsoft has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Incident Database restates.
